expert_role: City cultural planner acting as gatekeeper and source auditor (round 3, gate round)

findings.issue: Competition-project mode (private, no forks, no gallery or search, handles hidden, public sharing blocked) is the only thing that protects entrants from Terms cl. 4.1 and 5.1/5.3. The spec admits it 'needs platform-packet support', but it gives no fallback. M07 is core and ships to entrants. If the platform packet has not built private, unforkable projects by 13 Nov, an entrant who sets the VTC flag is working in the default platform mode: public, forkable, with handles. That is a disqualification risk the tool would have invited.
findings.fix: Add a hard release rule. The VTC entry flag can be enabled only after the platform packet confirms that private, no-fork and no-index work and has been tested (record the test date in M08). Otherwise the tool shows a fixed notice: do not create the competition project on the hosted platform; use local or offline mode, and export only through the M07 strip step. Add a metric: 'VTC flag available without verified private mode = 0'.

findings.issue: The ai_involvement-to-IPTC mapping misuses the vocabulary. IPTC defines compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia as 'Edited using Generative AI' (inpainting or outpainting) and compositeSynthetic as a mix of elements of which at least one is generative AI. algorithmicallyEnhanced is non-generative correction only. So 'composite' (AI elements combined with renders) should map to compositeSynthetic. Any 'assistive edit' that uses generative fill or upscaling should map to compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia, not algorithmicallyEnhanced. As written, the most common board workflow (a render with AI fill or entourage) would get a label that understates AI use. The spec calls that a breach of trust itself.
findings.fix: Remap as follows. none -> digitalCreation (renders) or humanEdits (edited captures). assistive non-generative -> algorithmicallyEnhanced. assistive generative edit -> compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia. composite with AI elements -> compositeSynthetic. generated -> trainedAlgorithmicMedia. Split the 'assistive edit' enum into generative and non-generative. Cite each term's IPTC definition and URI, and re-read the vocabulary at release, because terms are retired (for example, minorHumanEdits on 2024-09-17).

findings.issue: The spec treats the Public Views Guidelines (2024) as the place where per-view height rules live. The dataset's own metadata says the authoritative source for the corridors is the City's bylaws. The dataset was also modified on 19 Oct 2026 and is 'updated as needed', so the '24 records match the set kept on 10 Jul 2024' check is a snapshot that can go stale before 30 Nov. Entrants checking a touched cone would be pointed to the wrong instrument and could rely on an old cone set.
findings.fix: Point the 'rule to be checked' link to the applicable bylaw or official development plan as well as the Public Views Guidelines. Quote the dataset caveat ('authoritative source ... is the City's bylaws') on the cone table. Store the dataset modified date and the retrieval date with every run. Re-query total_count at each export and warn if it is not 24 or if the ids differ from the 10 Jul 2024 set.

findings.issue: The contact guard, eligibility check and Q&A card all rest on a fetch-tool summary of the Buildner jury page and the Terms. In three rounds no person has read either in a browser, and this round both URLs timed out. Clause numbers (3.3.5, 5.2, 8.3, 10.4, 10.10), the 1 Nov / 3 Nov dates and the juror names and firms are load-bearing. A wrong name or date would steer entrants into contact or a missed deadline. The City page adds that the City is the host and that the review contact is a named City planner. This makes the City the most likely Commissioning Party.
findings.fix: Before release, a person opens the jury page and the Terms in a browser, saves a dated PDF copy, and confirms every clause number, date and juror and firm string quoted in M01. Add a 'verified-by/date' field to the contact-guard card and block the card's release without it. Name City of Vancouver staff (including the Higher Buildings review team) explicitly in the no-contact list.

findings.issue: The VTC brief (S35) is still unopened after three rounds. The 30% weight, the cultural-context criterion wording, the anonymity clause and the site location all still come from the supplied summary. M07's strip rules and M08's three criterion items are built on that unread text. Registration closes 29 Oct, which is 8 days away, and only registered entrants can get the brief.
findings.fix: Make 'brief opened, version and date recorded' a release precondition for M07 export mode and M08, not a 13 Nov target. Register now if needed. If the brief's anonymity clause adds rules (for example file naming or board codes), add them to the M07 strip checklist before core.

findings.issue: The scope is honest, but core capacity is not credible as stated. The core subset (M01 stage A 3 days, M06 georeference and cone intersection 2 days plus ray casting 5, M07 9 days) comes to 14-19 person-days in 23 calendar days for two students who also own other packets. M07 also depends on PRES export and platform features from other packets. Entrants would get the tool 17 days before submission at best. There is no stated cut order inside M07 and no message to entrants about what will not arrive.
findings.fix: Publish an ordered cut list inside the core. 1) metadata strip and identity scan, 2) AI visible label plus the corrected IPTC term, 3) source-id lint, 4) glyph check, 5) PROV human_contribution and decided_by. Ray casting is formally v1. Show entrants a dated 'available now / not before 30 Nov' panel driven by the M08 entrant_scope record.

findings.issue: The claimable_by_entrant rationale says FPIC is obtained by States through Nations' institutions. TRC Call 92(i), which the packet already cites, asks the corporate sector to commit to meaningful consultation and to obtain FPIC before economic development projects. Entrants cannot claim FPIC because a hypothetical entry has no real project and no engagement. The reason is not that only States can obtain it.
findings.fix: Rewrite the rationale. UNDRIP Arts. 19 and 32(2) put the duty on States. TRC 92(i) asks companies to seek FPIC for real projects. A competition entry at N0-N3 has neither, so the FPIC claim stays locked. Keep the lock; correct the basis.

findings.issue: Status badges will be stale before submission. Shape Your City puts Phase 2 'draft policies' in Fall 2026 to Winter 2027, so draft Higher Buildings directions may appear before 30 Nov. On DRIPA, the April 2026 working group was to report by the fall 2026 legislative session, which is under way. The Wikipedia source was last edited 29 Sep 2026 and records no session events. The SCC hearing date and the BCCA neutral citation are still missing.
findings.fix: Re-check both badges at each release and on 25 Nov. Add BC Legislature bill status and the SCC docket as sources. Show the as-of date prominently, with 'may have changed: check' after 14 days.

findings.issue: S10 says the Musqueam page lists eight package items. The page also asks for 'additional documents' as Musqueam requires and says to contact Musqueam 'at the initial stages of project planning for all projects within Musqueam territory'. That sentence is the real reason applicability to ideas competitions is ambiguous, and the spec does not quote it.
findings.fix: Record nine items (eight named plus open-ended additional documents). Quote the 'all projects within Musqueam territory' line in the UNRESOLVED contact flag. Keep N0 as the default.

findings.issue: S54 attribution and S16 internal conflicts. 'No City approvals needed' is the reporter's statement in Global News, not the City's or the Nation's. The services list is the Mayor's quote. Wikipedia gives the tallest Sen̓áḵw tower as both 58 storeys and 56 storeys ('exempt from local height restrictions'), but M04 shows 58 without the conflict chip that its own rule requires.
findings.fix: Tag S54 facts by speaker (reporter vs Mayor). Add a 58 vs 56 conflict chip, or cite the Dezeen 12-58 figure as the source of 58.

findings.issue: S48 metadata is wrong. The page is 'Aboriginal Consultation and Accommodation - Updated Guidelines for Federal Officials to Fulfill the Duty to Consult - March 2011', a 2011 guideline for federal officials. It also says third parties 'do not have a legal obligation to consult', which is the clearest support for the 'consulted' ban and is not quoted.
findings.fix: Correct the title and year to 2011, mark it as federal-official guidance that may be dated, and quote the third-party line in the M01 ban-list basis.

findings.issue: The ethics check cites TCPS 2 and UBC's general student page. That page links a separate UBC 'Indigenous Research and Ethics Review' resource, which the spec does not open. It is directly relevant to the Indigenous reviewer and any Indigenous participants.
findings.fix: Open and cite the UBC Indigenous research ethics resource and add it to the instructor/BREB question list.

verdict: Round 3 handles most of the round 2 critique honestly. The entrant scope is cut to M01 stage A, M06 geometry and M07, and the review gate, the contact guard and the authorship fields are in place. It still fails the gate. M07's privacy mode, which entrants depend on, rests on platform features that are not built and has no fallback. The IPTC mapping understates generative AI use. M06 sends entrants to guidelines when the dataset says bylaws are authoritative, and treats a dataset updated on 19 Oct as fixed. The Terms, the jury list and the brief have still not been read by a person; I could not open the Buildner pages this round either. Fix these six conditions before entrants rely on it.
